data.one_liner: A Flutter plugin for controlling Bluetooth Low Energy, supporting central and peripheral roles.
data.what_it_does: Allows Flutter applications to act as both a central and peripheral Bluetooth Low Energy device. Provides comprehensive APIs for device discovery, connecting, reading/writing characteristics and descriptors, and advertising.
use_when: You need to build a Flutter app that communicates with BLE hardware peripherals.
Your application needs to act as a BLE peripheral device to broadcast services and data.
You require cross-platform BLE support across Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, and Linux.
avoid_when: You are developing and testing on emulators, as BLE does not work without physical hardware.
You need PeripheralManager support on Linux, which is currently unimplemented because bluez doesn't support it yet.
strengths: Supports both central and peripheral roles across multiple desktop and mobile platforms.
Provides fine-grained control over MTU, RSSI, characteristics, descriptors, and advertising.
weaknesses: PeripheralManager API is not implemented on Linux.
PeripheralManager advertising options have platform-specific limitations on Apple and Windows.
data.setup_notes: Requires physical devices for testing. On Android, ensure minSdk is 24 or higher and set up Bluetooth permissions in AndroidManifest.xml. On iOS/macOS, add usage descriptions and configure the app sandbox.
